Approximately twenty acres of riparian forest and upland buffers with native trees, shrubs, forbs and grasses comprise Bundy Brook. It also protects the water quality of the Fenton River and is an effective tool for controlling erosion and providing food and cover for wildlife.

Hungry World Farm is…

A PLACE of beauty and possibility. Our 175 acres includes 100 acres of forest, 10 acres of pasture, 2 acres of blueberries, ⅔ acre of market garden, and ½ acre of relic glacial hillside prairie. 

A COMMUNITY of soil organisms, trees, wildflowers, food-bearing plants, sheep, goats, chickens, cattle, bobcats, raccoons, deer, humans and a myriad of other creatures. 

EDUCATIONAL FARM practicing and teaching principles of regenerative agriculture as we produce vegetables, fruits, flowers, eggs, meat, and sourdough breads.  We invite neighbors near and far to learn alongside us and join us in seeking a healthy, hopeful world through regenerative food and agriculture.

A NONPROFIT ORGANIZATION seeking to nurture the soil and nourish people in mind, body and spirit. We celebrate and share the abundance of the land, while also working to restore what is out of balance or depleted.

listing_desc:
Rooted in tradition and proudly local, Little Pistol Farms offers a wide selection of fresh, homegrown produce straight from our fields to your table. From juicy tomatoes and crisp peppers to sweet melons, zucchini, squash, pickling cucumbers, beans, and a variety of hearty winter squash, everything we grow is nurtured with care and harvested at peak flavor.

Come fall, our fields transform into a 15-acre pumpkin wonderland, bursting with over 24 unique varieties—perfect for decorating, carving, and baking. Bring the whole family for a true U-pick pumpkin experience, where you can wander through the vines and pick your perfect pumpkin right off the stem.

Don’t forget to check out our delicious farm-made pumpkin products and keep an eye out—you might just spot one of our famous “great pumpkins!”

Whether you’re looking to fill your pantry or make lasting family memories, Little Pistol Farms invites you to experience the best of what each season has to offer.

listing_desc:
Al-Munir Farms is a vibrant urban agritourism destination in Newark, NJ, operated by Al-Munir LLC. Our two primary sites—Eden’s Farm in the South Broad Street neighborhood and Jannah on Grafton in the North Ward—offer immersive, educational, and culturally relevant experiences centered around food justice, ecological sustainability, and community wellness.

We host a wide range of public programs including farm tours, sustainable agriculture workshops, pollinator walks, community harvest events, and culturally affirming cooking demos. Our work is rooted in Black, Indigenous, and Afro-diasporic traditions, and features ethnobotanical crops from Africa, the Caribbean, Latin America, North America, and the Indian Subcontinent.

As a SARE-funded research site and participant in the USDA’s EQIP and SNAP-Ed programs, Al-Munir Farms also serves as a model for regenerative agriculture and community-led research. We welcome school groups, families, and civic organizations to visit us.

Non-food businesses are also welcome. The Market is held in Festival Market Square in downtown Battle Creek on Wednesday, 9-1, beginning in May and ending in October. Customers will find a family friendly market with a good variety of variety of vendors. Vendors will find a well managed and vendor friendly market. An open air marketplace under a pavilion offers picnic tables, restrooms onsite and free 1-hour parking for customers in the Hamblin Avenue ramp. Live music and other activities make summer fun at the farmers market. BCFM participates in Bridge Card (SNAP), Double Up Food Bucks, Senior Market FRESH, WIC Project FRESH, NHBP Elders Nutrition Program. listing_desc:
Cuyahoga Valley Farmers Markets’ (CVFM) works to provide access to and education about sustainable foods and agriculture to the communities in Northeast Ohio by building connections between our community with the producers of locally grown food. 
CVFM was established in 2022 to continue the operation of the long-running Countryside farmers markets in Howe Meadow and at Old Trail School, both located in the Cuyahoga Valley National Park. These vibrant farmers markets have been in operation since 2004 and have been growing steadily  since their inception.  
CVFM MARKET IMPACT:
During our Summer market in Howe Meadow (May-October) we connect on average 2,500 (peak 3,000) members of our community to producers of local food.
During our Winter market at Old Trail School (November-April) we have on average 600 shoppers per market (peak 1,000).
Provide consistent sales outlet for 70 local farms and businesses.
location_desc:

listing_desc: Common Ground Producers and Growers is a mobile farmers market and food hub. It is a family-run agricultural organization based in Wichita, Kansas, operating the state’s longest-running Mobile farmers market and food hub. Founded in 2014 by multi-generational farmer and CEO Donna Pearson McClish, the organization was established to eliminate food insecurity by delivering fresh, locally grown produce directly into neighborhoods with limited access to healthy food. Guided by the motto “All are fed. No one is hungry.” Common Ground operates on Pearson’s Family Farms—the largest Black-owned urban farm in the region. location_address: 131 East Main Street, McComb, OH, USA
listing_desc:
The McComb Farmers Market is more than a place to shop, it's a place where community grows. Each market brings together local farmers, bakers, artisans, and small businesses while creating a welcoming space for neighbors, families, and visitors to connect. Every purchase supports local entrepreneurs, strengthens our local economy, and helps preserve the small-town spirit that makes McComb special.

What truly sets our market apart is the experience. From live music and food trucks to our signature Sprouts Kids Club, every market offers something for all ages. Through hands-on activities, children learn about agriculture, nutrition, entrepreneurship, and healthy living while earning Sprout Bucks to spend with vendors, creating a fun and meaningful connection between kids and local businesses. The McComb Farmers Market isn't just about fresh food, it's about building relationships, supporting one another, and creating traditions that bring our community together.
location_desc:

From Findlay (20 minutes): Take State Route 15 West to McComb. Turn left onto Main Street (OH-235), continue into downtown, and you'll find the market on your left.

From Lima (35 minutes): Take State Route 65 North to State Route 613 West into McComb. Continue to Main Street, and the market will be in the Town Square.

From Bowling Green (35 minutes): Take I-75 South to Exit 159 (State Route 613). Head west on OH-613 into McComb and continue to downtown Main Street.

From Fostoria (25 minutes): Take State Route 23 South to State Route 613 West. Follow OH-613 into McComb until you reach the Town Square on Main Street.

Free parking is available on surrounding downtown streets and nearby public lots.

location_desc: Here are the directions for getting here from the Kona airport.  The Edge of the World is about 19 miles from Keohole (Kona) airport. Turn right on Rte. 19, which becomes Rte. 11 after Kailua-Kona town.  You\'ll pass the Manago Hotel (between 110 and 109 mile markers) on your right as you enter the small town of Capt. Cook.  On your left you\'ll pass the fire station, post office, and Kealakekua Ranch Center.  Two  streets past the Kona Theater, (the first street is  Anoi Place) maybe half a mile, you will make a right turn. (This turn is about 200 yards BEFORE the 109 mile marker.)  At that intersection you will see a one  foot by six foot wooden sign saying \"McCoy Plantation.\"  Turn right there and remain on that road for the next two tenths of a mile  (Don\'t drive down Coffee Drive.)(Please drive slowly from here to the Edge, as roads are narrow and visibility  poor.) After two tenths you will see a small  one foot by two foot sign with the number 82-5899, a two foot square sign that says \"Hale Mauka\" (not us but a good turning landmark),  and a white circle about two feet in diameter painted on the road.  Turn right there (it looks kind of like a driveway) and proceed down a narrow, lush (almost jungle-like, without elephants and tigers) road for two tenths of a mile.  You will pass two houses on your right,  just keep going straight ahead, down a hill, up a hill and out of the lushness with coffee plants on your left and a small pasture on your right.  When the pasture (and a low stone wall) end, you will turn right down the first cement driveway. You\'ll also see a six foot long white arrow painted in the road, and a small sign that says \"Edge\". It\'s a long driveway of about 400 feet,  Don\'t stop at the  first house on the right, or the second on the left which has a large green roof, just keep going until you come to The Edge of the World, where you\'ll see a very small sign.  You\'ll see a modern looking two story structure, upper floor is redwood with blue roof, and the lower level is beige stucco. If you feel confused, just give me a  call (808 328-7424), but our guests tell us the directions above are very good-- the road is just kind of bumpy about half way down the jungle road for 20 yards.  (Please remember to copy and bring these directions.) Directions from the SouthFrom the south, you\'ll be seeing mile markers indicating the distance from Hilo on the side of the road.  Approximately 100 yards after the 109 mile marker turn left (this is the first left after the 109 mm and also where you will find the McCoy Plantation sign).  The rest is the same as from the north.

We serve the greater Chattanooga community through education and advocacy programs that teach about growing food sustainably and choosing local produce. We produce sustainably-grown fruits, vegetables, and nursery stock, which we sell at the Main Street Farmers Market, at our seasonal on-site farm store, and to restaurants in downtown Chattanooga. Our Plant Sales, held in April and September each year, are a source of healthy-sustainably grown plant starts, live entertainment, and opportunities to shop for goods from local vendors. We treat our animals with respect and allow them to flourish in their natural environment and we are committed to their care. Our ruminant animals eat grass and cover crops for their entire lifetime. Any grains in our cover crop mix are grazed prior to grain formation. Chickens require grain and are fed organic grains along with fresh grass by moving their homes daily. Hormones, Pesticide, Vaccines and Wormer - none are ever given as they aren\'t needed with moves to fresh paddocks. Livestock have access to oilers filled with essential oils for fly and pest control. Our goal is to never administer antibiotics. Our customers never receive products that have been treated with an antibiotic.

We produce grass-fed beef and forest-raised pork while regenerating and restoring the land that we love using careful management.  We employ intensive rotational grazing in our pastures, generally moving our cattle herd to a new paddock every day.  Our cows are completely grass-fed from birth to finish.

  Our pigs are raised outdoors in a stress-free environment and forage for roots, nuts, insects, and plants on the forest floor. Their more varied diet, regular exercise, and exposure to sunlight result in more nutrient-dense meat that is much healthier for you, with a rich, delicious taste.

Our sacred aim is to cultivate this land to the best of our ability and to produce meat that is healthy for our families and the families of our customers.

Two Roots Farm has been growing vegetables, herbs, and flowers for the Roaring Fork Valley using regenerative methods since 2016. We aim to grow food in the cleanest, healthiest way possible: prioritizing the vitality of our farmers, soil, and eaters above all else. We use organic growing practices, minimum tillage, biodynamic compost, crop rotations, increased biodiversity, and sustainable methods to grow the best produce possible without the use of any chemicals, herbicides, or pesticides. location_desc:
14578 N Macy Millark Rd is a rural residential property in Macy, a small town in Allen Township, Miami County, Indiana (ZIP code 46951). Macy itself is a tiny community in northern Indiana, about 15 miles north-northwest of Peru, IN and about 9 miles southeast of Rochester, IN. 

The property sits along North Macy Millark Road, a rural county road that runs north–south through agricultural and lightly wooded land surrounding the town. The area has a mix of homes on large lots, farms, and open countryside typical of this part of Miami County. According to public data, the house at this address is a 3-bed, 1-bath single-family home on roughly 6.9 acres. 

Driving Directions
From Macy town center (around Main St / Columbia St):
Head north on N Main Street (also often State Road 19) out of the center of Macy.
Continue north until you reach Macy Millark Road (north of the town grid).
Turn left (west) onto N Macy Millark Rd.
Continue west/northwest along N Macy Millark Road for several miles (this is a rural road with few landmarks).
14578 N Macy Millark Rd will be on your left side (look for a rural residential driveway and house number sign).
This route keeps you on the main local roads serving the rural area around Macy. Exact distances can vary slightly depending on your starting point in town. It’s a sparsely populated area, so signage may be limited — using a GPS with the address entered is advisable for precise navigation.
